rules.condition: outline == OUTLINE_INVULNERABLE / OUTLINE_FLYING / OUTLINE_NAMED / team colour / else, each with its own priority chain
rules.semantic: A walker with several statuses blinks between their outlines, advancing one step per call from the outline it currently shows. From INVULNERABLE: flying wins (FLYING), else named-to-an-enemy-viewer (NAMED); then, unless NAMED was chosen, invisibility overrides to team colour (so invulnerable+flying+invisible shows team colour, and NAMED beats invisible only in this branch). From FLYING: named(enemy viewer) else invisible(team colour) else invulnerable. From NAMED: invisible else invulnerable else flying. From team colour: invulnerable else flying else named. Anything else: invisible, flying, invulnerable, named in that order. Named is shown only to a viewer of another team. Render-only value. In play the chain rarely advances past one step: living::act (living.cpp:179-180) does set_outline(0) EVERY sim tick for a living that is not invisible, so for a non-invisible living the chain restarts from the 'other (0)' arm each tick and the from-INVULNERABLE / FLYING / NAMED / team-colour arms are reached only between compute_outline calls inside one tick (several viewscreens or render frames per tick), or for invisible livings and non-living walkers whose outline persists. Some states leave the outline unchanged: from NAMED with only BIT_NAMED it stays NAMED (any viewer, including same-team); from FLYING with flight expired and only BIT_NAMED seen by a same-team viewer it stays FLYING; from INVULNERABLE with nothing else it stays INVULNERABLE.
